content:
The open-source Tessera project enables neat dashboards for Home Assistant on affordable 2.8-inch to 10.1-inch ESP32 touchscreen (development) kits from CYD, Guition, and Waveshare. The Tessera firmware adds a layer to ESPHome firmware for display management, touchscreen handling, dashboard rendering, tiles, plugins, and more. It works in conjunction with the Tessera Screen Manager, which provides the Home Assistant interface to configure screens, manage layouts, install firmware, and push updates. The whole solution is supposed to be easy to use thanks to a drag-and-drop editor, and users don’t need to know anything about YAML or MQTT. Tessera features highlights: Hardware support – Various ESP32 touchscreen platforms from 2.8-inch Cheap Yellow Displays (CYD) to 10.1-inch Guition panels. Drag-and-drop dashboard editor Configure screens, pages and tiles from Home Assistant. No YAML knowledge is needed. Multi-page dashboards – Organize controls across multiple pages Customizable layouts – Configure grid dimensions, tile sizes, icons, colours and [...]
